newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares edged up on Wednesday as the market gave out a collective sigh of relief after a modest overnight gain on Wall Street followed two days of successive heavy losses, dealers said.
But most players are still wary of recent jitters on the Dow and the local market came off its day highs as the afternoon wore on and U.S.-inspired nervous grew.

Dealers said they were watching weakness on the S&P 500 U.S. futures index for signs the Dow might start to continue its halted correction. Analysts in New York were expecting the market there to open lower.
"We came off towards the end a little as people concentrated on the Wall Street opening," said one dealer.

After a quick burst of gains in the morning South African shares trod water until noon and then gradually drifted away from their highs. The industrials index ended up 5.2 points at 8,179.8 as the all-share index put on 18.7 points to 6,981.1.

De Beers attracted heavy interest on good reaction to its higher Central Selling Organisation diamond sales and put on 350 cents to 160.25 rand. Other blue chips were mixed with SAB off 175 cents to 135.25 rand, while Anglo added 100 cents to 269.50 rand.

One curious market tale was a share price drop in cash shell Gentech on market rumours it was nearing a deal to put assets in the company. Industry sources told Reuters an announcement on a tie-up is due soon.
The stock hit a new year low of 32 cents as more than two million shares changed hands. The firm ended at 39 cents, down 15 cents.
Volumes were not huge, but came in at a healthy 623 million rands worth of shares being traded.

Dealers said the market was watching out for local money supply figures due at 1500 GMT, but was likely to be more strongly guided all week by events across the Atlantic, especially key U.S. payrolls data due on Friday.
"The market is going to be exceptionally cautious ahead of the U.S. unemployment figures," said Investec dealer Dominic Rey.

Gold shares had a jittery day as the gold prices failed to build convincingly on a mini-rally. The golds index added 5.2 points to 1,297.5 and individual shares had a mixed day with Western Deep losing 250 cents to 124.50 rand, Kloof adding 120 cents to 33.75 rand and Vaal Reefs putting on 125 cents to 265.75 rand.
South African share futures drifted through the day after a firm start and then took a late dip towards the end of the day on speculation of a Wall Street fall.
The all-share June contract was last at 6,360/75 from 6,380 as the industrials contract was at 7,930/40 from 7,943. The gold share contract was at 910/25 from 909.
